An increment is one single step of increase — a measured amount by which something goes up. It is not the total you reach; it is the specific amount of the rise itself.

Think of climbing a staircase. You don't teleport to the top — you go up one step at a time. Each of those individual steps upward is an increment. The staircase as a whole represents total growth; each individual step is one increment of that growth.
The three things that define it

It is always an increase, never a decrease. An increment adds something — it makes a number, an amount, or a quantity go up. Anything moving downward is the opposite (called a decrement), not an increment.

It refers to the amount of the increase, not the new total. If your salary goes from $50,000 to $52,000, your increment is $2,000. That is the step up. The $52,000 is simply your new salary — not the increment.

It is typically one step in a series of steps. The word is at its most natural when describing growth that happens gradually, in a sequence of additions. Each addition in that sequence is one increment.

Salary: When an employee receives a small, regular raise each year, that raise is called a salary increment. The increment is the specific amount their pay went up — say, $1,500.

Numbers and counting: If you count 10, 20, 30, 40 — each jump of 10 is one increment. You could equally count in increments of 5 (5, 10, 15, 20...) or in increments of 100. The increment is simply the size of each step.

Time: A doctor's office might schedule appointments in 20-minute increments — meaning slots are available at 9:00, 9:20, 9:40, and so on. Each 20-minute block is one increment of time.

Temperature: A thermometer is marked in increments of 1 degree — each tiny line on the scale is one degree of increase above the last.

A savings plan: If you save $300 every month toward a $3,600 annual goal, each monthly deposit is one increment toward that goal.

Software and technology: Programmers regularly talk about incrementing a value — meaning adding 1 (or some fixed amount) to a number each time a step in a process completes.
The deeper flavor of the word

"Increment" is not a neutral word. It carries the quiet suggestion that growth is happening in a controlled, deliberate, and measured way — not in one dramatic leap, but in careful, manageable steps.

This is why the word is popular in business, science, engineering, and policy. When a manager says "we'll implement these changes in increments," the message is: we are being thoughtful and cautious, not reckless. We are doing this step by step.

This also means the word subtly implies that each step is relatively small. While there is no rule that an increment must be tiny, in everyday use it leans toward modest, regular additions rather than enormous jumps.

"In small increments" means a little bit at a time. "Her confidence grew in small increments over the months."

"In fixed increments" means each step is the same size every time. "The price increases in fixed increments of $10."

"In increments of [number]" describes the exact size of each step. "The tank fills in increments of 5 litres."

"Salary increment" is a widely used phrase, especially in professional and corporate settings, to mean a periodic pay raise.

It is not a big, dramatic leap. The word carries a sense of modesty and regularity. A company tripling its revenue overnight would not normally be described as growth in increments.

It is not the result or the final total. It is only the step itself.

It is not a decrease. Never use increment to describe something going down.

The closely related adjective incremental means "happening gradually, in small steps." You will often hear it in phrases like "incremental progress" (progress that happens a little at a time) or "incremental improvement" (getting better, but modestly and steadily, not dramatically). Knowing this word helps you recognise the same idea across different sentence structures.

In one sentence: An increment is one specific, measured step of increase — the amount by which something goes up, as part of a gradual, step-by-step process of growth.
